newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nordic Inv Bank eyes Aug for Taiwan-dlr bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Nordic Inv Bank eyes Aug for Taiwan-dlr bond issue.

text.p: Nordic Investment Bank has scheduled its T$4 billion (US$143 million) Taiwan dollar-denominated bond issue for August, lead underwriter Citicorp International Securities said on Wednesday.

The bond would have a five-year term with annual interest payments and a coupon rate of approximately 0.28 percent plus the mid-rate of the yield of the Taiwan government bond series 85/3, Citicorp said in a statement.
Citicorp said the Nordic bank decided to make the issue because Taiwan's interest rates have been hovering at high levels.
"This is one of the advantages of this bond which makes it an attractive investment," Citicorp said.

Taiwan's overnight interbank rate soared above double digits in late June before easing in early July. But it still closed at a relatively high 7.208 percent on Wednesday, far outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
Nordic Investment Bank would become the fourth international bank to issue Taiwan-dollar bonds.
Nordic Investment Bank finances investment projects and exports of Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden.
The latest international bank to issue Taiwan-dollar bonds was the Central American Bank of Economic Integration, which made a T$6.8 billion issue on May 16.
The other two banks that have launched issues were the Asian Development Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
